transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Mark Santos (Hightower Head of ML), Alina Petrova (Platform), Devon Cole (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly standup to review latest benchmark artifacts comparing Redwood runtime vs incumbent provider. Tuning notes focused on batching, KV cache hit behavior, and quantization tradeoffs. Agreement to run extended head-to-head with updated configs; SOC2/infra items to be scheduled.

Topics:
- p50/p95 latency deltas
- sustained throughput and saturation points
- unit-cost per token & per-request economics
- routing/fallback and dedicated slot idea
- security/network questions (VPC peering, KMS)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um we'll keep this tight — 30 minutes ish plus Q&A, uh quick readout on the bench results we posted in the shared sheet.
[00:23] Mark: cool thanks Jordan, yeah we pulled up the sheet, saw the p95 numbers, quick question: are those with KV cache enabled on Redwood?
[00:32] Priya: yes, the main column labeled "RWD-quant-v3 (KV on)" is with prefix caching enabled — we also included a "KV off" variant in the next tab.
[00:44] Alina: got it, and baseline column is what our incumbent is doing today, right? IncumbentAI?
[00:50] Jordan: correct, IncumbentAI numbers came from your team-provided traces run on their recent infra, same prompts.
[01:05] Devon: small thing — our baseline had autoscale set to 8 to 32 instances, we matched that in the run. I just want to be sure apples-to-apples.
[01:17] Priya: we tried to mirror the orchestration. there were some differences in sequence length tail — incumbent had higher 99th token length because their client batches differently, so we normalized at 512 tokens for the main comparison.
[01:35] Mark: ok, numbers look promising but need context. can you walk p50/p95?
[01:42] Jordan: sure. short version — p50: incumbent 95ms, Redwood 78ms; p95: incumbent 430ms, Redwood 372ms. sustained throughput (steady-state small prompt workload): incumbent plateaued ~120 req/s, Redwood plateaued ~150 req/s under same GPU pool sizing. unit compute cost: incumbent estimated $0.0012/request (~$0.0009/token-equivalent), Redwood estimate $0.0008/request (~$0.0006/token-equivalent) given our batching and KV hit ratio assumptions.
[02:15] Mark: those p95 deltas are meaningful. what's driving it — smaller kernels / better batching?
[02:21] Priya: a few things — our kernel selection and fused attention path gives better per-token latency. also continuous batching at the runtime layer keeps utilization higher. KV cache hits reduce autoregressive decode steps for repeated prefixes — we saw hit-rate at ~82% in your workload, incumbent reported ~60%.
[02:45] Devon: were those runs with quantized weights? we worry about quality vs perf.
[02:50] Priya: the main column is int8 quantized with our calibration. we included a float16 baseline, and quality regression on our eval prompts stayed within the pass threshold (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy on your QA set). we can share the diff deck. small hallucination/perf tradeoffs were observed on edge prompts.
[03:12] Alina: do you support on-prem private deployment? we might need VPC peering for token/data residency.
[03:18] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private. for pilots we can do VPC peering + customer-managed KMS. we'll follow up with SOC2 docs & network runbook.
[03:28] Mark: any flaky tail latency spikes? p99s?
[03:33] Priya: p99 for incumbent was ~920ms, Redwood p99 ~760ms in these runs. spikes tied to cold KV warms and occasional batching inefficiencies under bursty arrival. We have a mitigation plan: pre-warming top prefixes and a small dedicated warm pool reduces p99 by ~120ms in our lab.
[03:58] Devon: that warm pool sounds like dedicated slots — cost delta?
[04:03] Jordan: yes it's basically reserving a couple GPUs (or dedicated instances) during peak windows. rough ballpark for your peak usage pattern — 2 dedicated slots would add around $2.5k/month on top of usage; but they improve 95/99 significantly. We'll produce a scenario spreadsheet.
[04:20] Mark: can you run a quick sensitivity — batch size from 1 to 16 and quantization off/on? we want to see quality impact plus latency.
[04:26] Priya: yes, that's in this week's lab plan. we'll do a batch sweep and send the raw logs.
[04:33] [short crosstalk — 'yeah' / 'thanks']
[04:40] Jordan: ok moving on — one surprising bit was token cost. we saved ~33% on unit token cost due to better batching and higher KV hit. that reduces cost per 1M tokens by a notable margin.
[04:55] Alina: curious about multi-model routing: sometimes we fallback to a smaller cheaper model for low-risk queries. do you support automatic fallback?
[05:02] Priya: yes, routing policies by intent/confidence are supported. can configure per-route model families, with a fallback chain. we can demo a canary traffic split too.
[05:11] Mark: what about compliance — audit logs and retention?
[05:15] Jordan: we have retention settings in the console, full audit logs for dedicated/private tiers, and integrations to your SIEM. will attach SOC2 plus the data retention table.
[05:26] Devon: on the infra side, need to confirm IP allowlist and peering CIDR, who owns that action?
[05:31] Alina: I can take it. I'll confirm peering windows and share our security contact.
[05:36] Alina: (sigh) also can we get an architecture diagram for VPC-peered private control plane?
[05:41] Jordan: yes. I'll include a network runbook doc link in the follow-up.
[05:47] Priya: back to bench — we noticed incumbent has slightly better cold-start p50 in one off-case because they have lower contention for shared IO on their infra, but overall the steady-state favors Redwood. If we remove KV caching, the gap shrinks.
[06:10] Mark: interesting. so the big lever is KV cache + batching. can you quantify through a table?
[06:15] Priya: yep — short table from today's runs:
- Redwood (KV on, batch auto): p50 78ms, p95 372ms, throughput 150 rps, unit-cost ~0.0008/request
- Redwood (KV off, batch auto): p50 110ms, p95 510ms, throughput 130 rps
- Incumbent (baseline): p50 95ms, p95 430ms, throughput 120 rps, unit-cost ~0.0012/request
[06:45] Devon: those numbers align with what we saw. is the latency measured end-to-end including network?
[06:50] Jordan: yes we included simulated egress latency to approximate production. we also included a pure-infra column (no client-side network) in the appendix.
[07:00] Mark: any anomalies in error rates?
[07:04] Priya: error rate was low — incumbent had ~0.08% transient 5xx vs Redwood ~0.03% in the run window. we did see some client-side retry storms during our largest bursts; we recommend jittered backoffs.
[07:20] Alina: about the head-to-head: will Redwood run the test in Hightower's account or in Redwood's sandbox?
[07:25] Jordan: for the definitive head-to-head, we suggest running both providers from the same client environment. Priya can run the Redwood side in your staging VPC via private endpoint. you'll run incumbent in the same environment so network is equalized.
[07:39] Mark: ok that works. timeline?
[07:41] Priya: we can schedule the 10k-run within 48 hours once we get the green light and your staging creds.
[07:48] Mark: we'll triage creds and share them by monday.
[07:53] Devon: quick question on quantization pipeline — do you provide model accuracy checks automatically or do we need to run our own eval harness?
[07:59] Priya: both — we provide a quantization report (per-layer calibration deltas) and a quick eval harness. but we recommend you run the canonical QA prompts to be safe.
[08:10] Jordan: also, note that model variant differences can be pinned per route — so you can test on smaller models for lower risk traffic.
[08:18] Alina: about pricing — is that estimate including reserved capacity discounts?
[08:22] Jordan: no, the estimate in the sheet is on-demand. reserved/dedicated discounts would be applied at contract stage — we can model committed usage scenarios.
[08:30] Mark: let's talk about next week's milestones. we want: 1) head-to-head 10k sweep, 2) quantization quality report, 3) SOC2 docs & VPC runbook. Are there blockers?
[08:42] Jordan: no blockers on our side. Priya: we'll need the staging creds and a short list of canonical prompts.
[08:48] Mark: sending creds and canonical prompt set by EOD Friday.
[08:52] [pause, typing sounds]
[09:00] Priya: one more technical note — we observed that reducing batch max latency window from 80ms to 40ms lowered p95 by ~30ms at cost of 6% throughput; depending on your SLA we can tune for latency or cost.
[09:17] Devon: that tradeoff is useful. in our case p95 < 400ms is target. can you aim to hit that with the warm pool + batch window tweak?
[09:25] Priya: yes — preliminary lab shows warm pool + 40ms batch window gets p95 about 360-380ms typically. we'll include that config in the head-to-head.
[09:36] Mark: perfect. last thing — action owners and dates?
[09:40] Jordan: action items in the follow-up, but quick recap: Jordan send perf spreadsheet (due Mon), Priya run 10k head-to-head (due Tue), Alina share peering window and security contact (due Mon), Devon share orchestration config (due today).
[09:56] Alina: I'll get you the peering window; please include the network diagram and the KMS integration notes.
[10:02] Jordan: will do. any other concerns?
[10:06] [small chatter]
[10:12] Mark: no, looks good. excited to see the head-to-head.
[10:16] Jordan: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet, raw logs link, and SOC2 package.
[10:21] Priya: I'll start the bench run, expect raw logs in Slack and the S3 bucket link.
[10:26] Meeting end.

References and artifacts mentioned: perf_spreadsheet_q3.xlsx (drive link), raw_logs_s3://hightower-pilot/redwood-run-20260911, SOC2_summary_v2.pdf (link to docs), network_runbook_draft.pdf

Note on transcription: some words mis-transcribed (K V vs KV, occasional proper-noun errors). Speakers sometimes overlap; timestamps are approximate.
